Formulation  
Patient, a child aged approximately 7–8 years (DOB 2016), presents with physical symptoms consistent with an acute respiratory illness (sore throat, dry cough, mild shortness of breath) accompanied by anxiety related to health concerns and family history of lung cancer. Predisposing factors include family history of serious illness. Current stressors are physical illness symptoms and associated health anxieties. Protective factors include absence of mental health issues, no substance use, and engagement with care. Mental health concerns are limited to situational anxiety related to physical illness.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Anxiety related to physical illness and health concerns  
- Patient Goal(s): To receive reassurance about physical health and reduce anxiety about serious illness  
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide accurate information and reassurance; monitor anxiety symptoms; support coping during illness recovery  
- Actions (Patient): Engage in relaxation/coping strategies (not directly recorded but implied need for reassurance)  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance regarding diagnosis (expectation of viral illness recovery); offer sick note; advise on symptom monitoring and follow-up if worsening; discuss red flags for urgent review  

Secondary Problem: Not applicable  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
  Topics Covered: Nature of current respiratory illness; expected course and recovery timeline; importance of rest, fluids, and symptomatic care; warning signs requiring urgent care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased or sudden shortness of breath; worsening cough; new or increased chest pain; persistent symptoms beyond expected recovery period  
- Coping Strategies: Rest, hydration, paracetamol for symptom management; recommended follow-up if symptoms worsen
